I scanned the codebase and these three items line up with what you’re seeing. Here’s how they’re wired today and why the behavior matches your feedback:

**Findings**
- **“If/then” in company context isn’t a real feature yet.** The app treats company context as plain text and injects it into the system prompt; there’s no structured rule parsing or enforcement. That means “if x then y” is just another sentence the model may or may not follow. The live chat path uses `api.ai.chatCompletions.generateChatResponse` and only passes a long system prompt with `companyContext` (no rule engine, no retrieval). See `convex/messages/mutations.ts` and `convex/ai/chatCompletions.ts`. The vector-store path in `convex/ai/assistants.ts` is not used by the chat-completions flow, so putting rules there won’t make them more reliable.
- **The “short sound” is coming from the hook + conversation detail, not from OS notifications.** New-customer sounds fire in `app/components/support/conversation-detail.tsx` and audio is created in `app/hooks/use-sound-notifications.ts`. The mute toggle only gates future `playSound` calls and doesn’t stop a sound already triggered, so a quick “blip” can still occur if the sound is fired and then muted or if state lags a render cycle. There’s no separate desktop suppression or global setting wiring here.
- **“Resolve” does not close the ticket; it only marks status and allows auto‑reopen.** `markIssueResolved` sets status to `"resolved"` but `sendCustomerMessage` immediately auto‑unresolves and reopens the same conversation when the customer replies. The UI even hints this: “customer can send a message to reopen.” See `convex/conversations/mutations.ts`, `convex/messages/mutations.ts`, and `app/components/support/conversation-detail.tsx`. Customer chat doesn’t block input on resolved status either (`app/components/customer/customer-chat-detail.tsx`).
